newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N.-Iraq sanctions panel to meet Mon, agenda slim.
newsitem.headline: U.N.-Iraq sanctions panel to meet Mon, agenda slim.

text.p: A scheduled meeting of the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq set for 1530 EDT (1930 GMT) Monday is not expected to be more than a routine gathering covering technical issues, Western diplomats said.
Potential items of interest pending from the panel's previous meeting in late August have become muted.
The question of allowing Turkey to buy Iraqi oil in compensation for the economic hardship it has incurred since sanctions were imposed on Baghdad in 1990 is a non-starter, panel diplomats said.

Last week, the United Nations said it was still not satisfied that minimum conditions existed in the north for the start of the plan, which alows Iraq partial oil sales worth $2 billion every six months to buy civilians food and aid for relief from punishing sanctions.

The U.N. decision came before the latest spate of inter-Kurdish fighting between forces of the Iraqi-backed Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), allied with Iran.

Further, the sanctions committee will not review allegations made by the United States at the last meeting, in which Washington said Iran was helping Iraq to bust sanctions by permitting gasoil shipments through its waters.
Diplomats said the United States had not come forward with a report on the matter. A spokesman for the U.S. delegation said the report detailing charges against Iran was not ready.
After the committtee reviewed U.S. allegations in August, it requested the statistical, photographic and other proof be put into written form before further action was considered.
